TF-C81 (D-CSUBSET-ALWAYSINLINE): GNU `__attribute__((always_inline))` is HONORED — the source directive reaches a real sink (`attributeSemantics.effects` verb `alwaysInline` -> SymbolRecord.isAlwaysInline -> HirAlwaysInlineMap -> MirFunc.alwaysInline -> the inliner's §2.9 legality gate, rule 6) — and the honoring COMPOSES with the SHIPPED release optimizer across all four targets. FIVE spellings appear in one program: mode-2 (after the type), mode-3 (specifier prefix), the dunder form `__always_inline__`, ★ the SQLITE shape `__attribute__((always_inline)) inline` (exactly what `SQLITE_INLINE` expands to, composing with the C99 `inline` specifier TF-C79 landed), and PROTOTYPE-ONLY (definition bare, reaching MIR solely through the post-Pass-1.5 proto/def OR-merge). add_five(0)=5 -> times_two=10 -> minus_three=7 -> plus_one=8 -> declared_first=8; wide(8) is a fixed nonzero constant, so the program exits 42.
★★ WHAT THIS EXAMPLE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM — the same honest split `noinline_attribute` uses. Inlining is SEMANTICS-PRESERVING, so NO exit code can distinguish inlined from not-inlined, and every runtime probe that appears to (function-address comparison, stack-depth measurement) either invokes undefined behavior or TAKES THE CALLEE'S ADDRESS — which makes the inliner refuse under §2.9 rule 4 instead, rendering the check vacuous. Rather than ship a check that cannot fail, this example witnesses the COMPOSITION (five spellings parse, reach the sink, and the resulting SPLICE still yields a correct runnable program under the real shipped pipeline on every target; a bypass that mis-threaded an argument, cloned a block wrongly or desynchronized the call graph lands here as a wrong exit code on four targets at once), and the APPLIED FACT is asserted where it is observable — at MIR tier by `MirLoweringCLinkage.AlwaysInlineBypassesThresholdInShippedRelease` (which loads release.pipeline.json BY NAME and asserts the Call instruction is GONE), its non-vacuous twin `OverThresholdCalleeWithoutAlwaysInlineKeepsItsCall` (which PROVES the callee genuinely exceeds the threshold rather than assuming it), `Inlining.AlwaysInlineCalleeBypassesCostThreshold` + its flag-clear twin, and `MirRebuildHelper.RebuildFunctionPreservesAlwaysInline`.
★ THE OVER-THRESHOLD DESIGN IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT INCIDENTAL. `wide()` is far larger than the shipped release `inlineThreshold` (50), so the release arm exercises the cost-model BYPASS rather than an inline that would have happened anyway. MEASURED on a real arm64 binary: the identical program WITHOUT the attribute keeps `bl _sym_75` inside `main`; WITH it that call is absent and only the entry trampoline + `_exit` calls remain.
★ WHAT `always_inline` DOES NOT PROMISE IN DSS, said here because the name overpromises: it EXEMPTS THE CALLEE FROM THE SIZE THRESHOLD and nothing else. Every correctness refusal still wins (Weak binding, same-SCC recursion, address-escape, no returning path, arity/type mismatch) and DSS is SILENT when one of them refuses — a conservative divergence from GCC (which errors) and clang (which warns). And it is scoped to the INLINER, not the program: under the shipped `debug` pipeline (`Identity` only) there is no cost model to bypass, so the attribute is VACUOUS and every call stays out-of-line. GCC and clang honour it at -O0 because their inliner always runs; DSS's does not. That asymmetry is stated in the `c.lang.json` effects row AND pinned by `MirLoweringCLinkage.AlwaysInlineIsInertUnderShippedDebugPipeline`, so the config claim and the behaviour cannot drift apart.
★ RED-ON-DISABLE, re-verified against the FINAL build, TWO ways — AND THEY BEHAVE DIFFERENTLY, WHICH IS THE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE FEATURE. (a) Delete the `&& !mir.funcAlwaysInline(callee)` clause from `inlining.cpp` rule 6: `Inlining.AlwaysInlineCalleeBypassesCostThreshold` and `MirLoweringCLinkage.AlwaysInlineBypassesThresholdInShippedRelease` both go red. (b) Keep the clause and drop ONLY the `src_.funcAlwaysInline(oldFn)` argument in `mir_rebuild_helper.cpp`: the end-to-end release pin stays COMPLETELY GREEN, and exactly two flag-survival assertions fail (`MirRebuildHelper.RebuildFunctionPreservesAlwaysInline` plus the survives-the-rebuild check inside the inlining unit test). ★ THAT IS THE OPPOSITE OF TF-C78's `noinline` RESULT, where the same hop produced byte-identical end-to-end breakage. The reason is structural: a `noinline` flag must keep REFUSING on every one of the release pipeline's 4 iterations, so clearing it re-arms the inliner on iteration 2; an `alwaysInline` flag only has to survive to the FIRST inlining opportunity, and `Inlining` runs first in iteration 1 before any rebuild touches the module. So for this feature the end-to-end pin does NOT subsume the propagation pin — it is BLIND to that hop, and the dedicated pin is the only thing that catches it. The flag still matters wherever iteration 1 does not finish the job (a callee that becomes inlinable only after an earlier pass simplifies its caller; a cross-CU module merged post-optimization), which is why the hop is carried rather than argued away. This example itself stays green under BOTH disable states, exactly as its `noinline` sibling does, and says so rather than implying otherwise.
★ The `release` arm is MANDATORY, not decoration: this is an optimizer×feature composition, and a baseline-only example would leave the one interaction that matters unwitnessed.
★ The whole file is VERIFIED clang-clean (`-fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -isysroot $(xcrun --show-sdk-path)`, zero errors, zero warnings) and the clang -O2 binary independently exits 42, so the expected exit code is ground truth from a real toolchain rather than merely what DSS happens to produce. All arithmetic in `wide()` is UNSIGNED because the body deliberately overflows; signed overflow would be undefined behavior.
